lesson_title: Paper 1 Essentials: Macroeconomics and Economic Pursuits in One Sweep
hook_text: Paper 1 is the most predictable exam you will ever write. Here's its skeleton.
clip_script: Economics Paper 1 never changes its skeleton — only the numbers move. Thirty compulsory objective marks. Then three forty-mark questions and you answer TWO. Then two essays and you write ONE. That's it — you never answer everything, you answer what you trained for. So train the sure things. The multiplier: one divided by one minus the mpc. Spend sixty cents of every rand? One over 0,4 — the multiplier is 2,5, and a R10 billion injection becomes R25 billion of income. The rand: just supply and demand for dollars. Importers buy dollars, exporters bring them home — more imports, the dollar costs more rands, the rand weakens. And a weak rand is never one-sided: exporters and tourism smile while petrol and medicine bite. The Laffer curve: tax at nought percent, earn nothing; tax at a hundred, earn nothing; the peak lives in between. And the growth plans are five words on a timeline — houses, discipline, skills, jobs, 2030. Walk in knowing the skeleton, and Paper 1 stops being a mystery.
visual_style: An exam paper unfolding into a skeleton diagram; a rand coin on a see-saw against a dollar; spending rounds rippling outward from one R10 billion splash; a timeline of five milestones stamping down in order.
pacing: Brisk march through the structure, a beat on each formula, a steady landing on the five-word timeline.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision session and walk into Paper 1 with the whole skeleton in your head.
